errors: 'um -2πi' as the jump of the imaginary part n is a slip: n is real, so its jump is -2π. The jump of t = m+ni is -2πi (the published text and the previous page state the jump for the complex function).

'nimmt ... jedenfalls nur ab' (if the transcription is right) contradicts the sign reasoning. With ∂n/∂s = -∂m/∂p and m not increasing inward (∂m/∂p ≤ 0), n is non-decreasing along the positively oriented boundary. This also matches the next sentence: n runs through all values up to one 2π larger. Either Riemann's slip or a misreading ('zu' vs 'ab').

Gap (period-typical): monotonicity is argued only as non-strict (∂m/∂p ≤ 0). Strict monotonicity (Hopf lemma) or a degree argument via Art. 7 is needed for injectivity on the boundary. Boundary regularity of T is tacitly assumed.
Unjustified step by modern standards: existence of the minimiser in the Dirichlet principle is assumed (Weierstrass's later criticism), as is finiteness of the defect integral for the chosen α+βi.

results.what: Every simply connected Riemann surface with boundary maps conformally onto the unit disc, uniquely once an interior point and a boundary point are normalised
Construction of the analytic function t with Re t=0 on the boundary and a logarithmic pole at z0, obtained by minimising the Cauchy-Riemann defect integral
results.modern_name: Dirichlet principle / Green's function with pole
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (named after Dirichlet), Green, Gauss, Thomson

results.what: Re t ≤ 0 inside by the maximum principle, and monotonicity of the conjugate along the boundary from ∂n/∂s = -∂m/∂p
results.modern_name: maximum principle for harmonic functions; boundary behaviour of Green's function

results.what: The mapping function is w = exp(-g - i·g*), normalised by a rotation; a branch point at the centre is handled by (1/n)log(z-z0)
results.modern_name: conformal map via Green's function, f = exp(-(g + i g*))

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of Art. 21 of Riemann's published 1851 dissertation (the Riemann mapping theorem via the Dirichlet principle). The content is well known as his and the draft differs only in small wording and sign slips.

checkable.asserts: Model case T = unit disc: w = e^t = (z-a)/(1-conj(a) z) has modulus 1 on the boundary, i.e. m = Re t = 0 there (expected 0).
m = log|(z-a)/(1-a z)| is harmonic away from the pole (expected 0).
For T = unit disc, z0=0: radial derivative of m = log r is 1 > 0, so m decreases inward (∂m/∂p ≤ 0 with p the inner normal) and n = th increases along the positive boundary; the circuit gain is 2π.
Branch-point case: w = exp((1/n) log(z-z0)) is a single-valued local uniformiser of a branch point of order n-1 (expected 0).

transcription_corrections: Lines 1-3 are likely 'durch Hinzufügung einer bis auf einen bloss imaginären constanten Theil bestimmten veränderlichen complexen Grösse, welche am Rande bloss imaginär ist'. The '[?] von [?] ... [?]' should be read in that sense (determined up to an imaginary constant).
'O_0' is probably just 'O' (the point corresponding to z0); likewise 'dass O auf den Mittelpunkt des Kreises verlegt wird'.
'nimmt ... jedenfalls nur ab': the logic requires 'zu' (increase). Check the manuscript; if it really reads 'ab', it is Riemann's slip.
'um -2πi' for the jump of n is as written in the manuscript (Riemann's slip), not a transcription error.
Final line of the paragraph: probably 'deren weitere Ausführung man mir indess mit Art. 14 leicht erlassen wird'.
'ein Max. innerhalb' is probably 'ein Maximum im Innern'.
